answer: notes, starting from Newton’s second law. It says we split horizontal and vertical: m x double dot equals zero, m y double dot equals minus m g. And initial conditions: x and y start at zero, velocities are v naught cos theta and v naught sin theta. Then it integrates to get x dot of t and x of t: x of t equals v naught cos theta times t. Sure. Sure. So we're setting up standard projectile motion. The horizontal equation says no acceleration, so x double dot is zero. title: Alex's 'mm-hmm' and 'right' don't stop or restart its explanation
idealItem: Cross-cutting: knowing when to talk + Done-feel 1
asked: Explain this first part to me in four or five sentences. || Mm-hmm. || Right.
answer: We split the motion into horizontal and vertical because they don't affect each other. Horizontally, no force means no acceleration, so the horizontal velocity just stays constant. Vertically, gravity pulls down with acceleration minus g. The initial speed is split into v naught cos theta horizontally and v naught sin theta vertically. From that, integrating gives horizontal position growing linearly in time. x equals v naught cos theta times t. And the vertical velocity starts at v naught sin theta and then decreases linearly with g.
